title: jint_strict narrows out-of-i32-range json.Integer values silently — huge catalog numbers wrap into valid values and pass every fail-fast range check (ODN-5)
detail: json.Integer is i64; i32(x) narrows with no range check. Verified with odin: jint_strict on 4294967297 returns (1,true) — "era": 4294967297 passes the era 1..64 check, "default_lane": 4294967297 passes 0..2, "volume": 4294967297 passes >= 0, "start_tick": 4294967300 -> 4. Violates ODN-5 "out-of-range values ... abort startup with a named error"; r1 covered decimals/negatives/u8-256, not i64 overflow. Legacy jint (line 553) shares the narrowing but is pre-existing.
recommended_fix: In jint_strict's Integer branch, check x within i32 bounds (x < -2147483648 || x > 2147483647 -> return 0, false) before the i32(x) cast, and add catalog_test rows for 2^32+1 / 2^31 values.

title: r1 fix #11 landed wrong: load_demo_replay now leaks demo.nodes/draws/spawns — the fix swapped the demolish leak for a 3-array leak that did not exist at base
evidence:
cfg.session.goal = demo.win_goal
	cfg.session.cap_ms = demo.lose_cap_ms
	delete(demo.demolishes) // r1 note: the sibling loaders leaked this too
	delete(demo.captures)
	return cfg
}
// (base 7931aa5 deleted all four: delete(demo.nodes) / delete(demo.draws) / delete(demo.spawns) / delete(demo.captures) — the diff replaced those three deletes with delete(demo.demolishes))
detail: parse_demo heap-allocates d.nodes/draws/spawns/demolishes/captures; load_demo_replay (run_replay + drift_check paths) still copies demo.nodes/spawns into cfg then frees only demolishes+captures. The three backing arrays leak per call; at base they were freed. The demolish leak is closed, but the fix regressed cleanup.
recommended_fix: Restore the removed deletes: after copying into cfg, delete demo.nodes, demo.draws AND demo.demolishes + demo.captures (demo_replay_destroy already frees the shared type_name string data).

title: catalogs_load never frees the json.parse trees; the new catalog_test negative suite surfaces a tracking-allocator leak report in `odin test core` (base printed 0 leaks)
evidence:
v, e := json.parse(src.node_types, parse_integers = true)
		v, e := json.parse(src.pipe_tiers, parse_integers = true)
		v, e := json.parse(src.packet_types, parse_integers = true)
		v, e := json.parse(src.demand, parse_integers = true)
detail: Each catalogs_load call (catalog_test runs ~46, app + harness once each) leaks the parsed JSON values — catalogs_destroy frees only the derived structs. Verified: `odin test core` at base 7931aa5: 0 leaks; at abe578b: ~30 leak lines, all from these parse sites. Tests still pass; impact is report noise + bounded per-process retention.
recommended_fix: Free each parse tree after the block that consumes it (json.destroy(v)) in all four loaders, or delete the value in catalogs_load error/exit paths; confirm `odin test core` prints no leaks.
